2026-12-24.title: Thursday after the Sunday before Yaldo · Eve of Yaldo
readings: God's power seen in what he has made
2026-12-24.alt: Eve of Yaldo (Christmas). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast ends with the festal Holy Qurbono of Yaldo.
2026-12-24.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: On the eve of Yaldo the prologue reaches its summit: “And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory.” The Greek says he “pitched his tent” among us, like the tabernacle in the desert filled with God's glory. From his fullness we have all received “grace upon grace”. The law came through Moses; grace and truth through Jesus Christ. “No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.”

Paul's words to the Romans are sobering: God's eternal power and divine nature have been visible in creation from the beginning, yet human beings exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal things. Christmas is God's answer to our idolatry: no longer an image made by human hands, but the true Image of God, born of a woman, lying in a manger. Tonight the whole Church kneels before him.
outline: What would you prepare if God came to stay at your house?
God pitches his tent among us.
“The Word became flesh and lived among us.”
live: If possible, make your confession today and come to the Yaldo Qurbono.
Let the gifts and food tomorrow be at the service of Christ, not the centre.
2026-12-24.prayer: Word made flesh, you pitched your tent among us and showed us the Father's glory. As we keep the vigil of your birth, fill us with grace upon grace, and make our hearts a fitting dwelling for you. Amen.
altar: Tonight at the Holy Qurbono the Word made flesh is given to us. From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.

quick: The Word became flesh and lived among us.
From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.
Christ is the true Image of God, not an idol.
2026-12-24.action: Come to the festal Qurbono of Yaldo with a prepared heart.
2026-12-24.question: Is my heart ready to receive him tomorrow?

family.explain: The Word became a human being and lived among us. Jesus shows us exactly what God is like.
family.intention: We pray for all families gathering tonight, and for those who are alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift will each of us give to Jesus tonight?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Word made flesh, full of grace and truth, on this Eve of Yaldo we wait for you with joy. Enlighten our hearts. Amen.
share: Paul says humanity exchanged God's glory for images (Romans 1:23). What false images take God's place in my life?
The Word became flesh (John 1:14). What does it mean to me tonight that God became man?
What grace upon grace have I received this year?
interc: For the Church throughout the world on this holy night.
For families gathering for Yaldo, that they may be united in love.
For those alone, sick or grieving tonight.
For the poor and homeless, who share the poverty of Bethlehem.
For peace in the Holy Land and throughout the world.
pm.close: Lord God, your only Son has made you known. Fill us tonight with grace upon grace, and let your Word dwell in our hearts and homes. Amen.

illus: In a small Malankara parish in the high ranges, the electricity failed during the service of Yaldo. The priest continued by candlelight. An old woman said afterwards: “It was as if we were in the cave of Bethlehem, with only the light of the Child.”

homily: Dear friends, on the Eve of Yaldo St Paul speaks frankly about the human condition: the wrath of God is revealed against all ungodliness and wickedness of those who by their wickedness suppress the truth. Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature have been understood and seen through the things he has made (Romans 1:18, 20).

Paul says that humanity knew God through creation but did not honour him: they became futile in their thinking, and their senseless minds were darkened. They exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images (Romans 1:21–23). This is why the world needed a Saviour.

The Gospel gives God's answer: the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth. From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known (John 1:14–18).
Humanity exchanged God's glory for images. Tonight, God gives us the true image of himself: a Child in a manger. Humanity's darkened mind is enlightened by the Word made flesh.

Tonight our parishes will celebrate the service of Yaldo with joy. The fast ends. Stars shine on our homes. But let us not lose the heart of the feast: God has come close. The invisible God has become visible.
Before the celebrations begin, let us find a quiet moment to kneel before the crib and say: Lord, you came for me. Thank you. Let us receive tonight grace upon grace. A blessed Yaldo to all. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight Jesus, the Son of God, is born as a little baby! Welcome Him with joy and tell Him you love Him.

sub: The Word pitched his tent among us.
q: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Come to the Yaldo Qurbono with a prepared heart.

sub: The Lord is merciful and gracious.
From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.
q: The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Thank God for three graces received this year.

sub: God's power is seen in what he made.
q: The heavens are telling the glory of God; and the firmament proclaims his handiwork.
Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature, invisible though they are, have been understood and seen through the things he has made.
points.apply: Keep Christ, not things, at the centre of Christmas.

concl: God has pitched his tent among us.
Let us kneel before him tonight.
